Coram:
The Hon'Ble Ms. Justice J.M.Khazi
Oral Order

(PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI) This petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is by accused No.1, seeking quashing criminal proceedings initiated against him in crime No.230/2023 of Kudligi PS pending on the file of the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and JMFC, Kudligi for the offence punishable under Section 19(1) of the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act, 2007 ('the Act'
for short).
2.
In support of the petition, the petitioner has contended that the very registration of the FIR against the petitioner is contrary to the provisions of the Act.

Section 19-A of the Act which deals with cognizance of the offences prohibit the court taking cognizance of offence under the Act except on a written complaint filed by the Registration and Grievance Redressal Authority or any officer authorized in this behalf by the Registration and Grievance Redressal Authority.

Contrary to the said NC: 2024:KHC-D:16539 provision, instead of filing a private complaint, the Medical Officer,
Kugligi Taluk has given first information report and on that basis, the concerned police have registered the case and proceed with the investigation and pray to allow the petition.
3. Respondent-State is represented by the learned HCGP.

4. Heard arguments and perused the records.
5.
The Medical Officer, Kudligi Taluk has given first information stating that petitioner/accused without possessing requisite medical certificate was running a clinic.

On 29.11.2023, on receipt of the said information, he along with the concerned police and witnesses conducted raid on the house of the petitioner and found that he is running a clinic and kept all the necessary medical instruments, tablets, stethoscope, syrup etc.
He admitted that he is not holding any degree to run the medical practice.
Therefore, the entire materials found in NC: 2024:KHC-D:16539 his possession are seized through mahazar and report is given.
6. Based on the said report, the concerned police have registered crime in crime No.230/2023 of Kudligi PS for the offence punishable under Section 19(1) of the Act and taken up investigation.
It is being challenged in the present petition.

7. As rightly submitted by the learned counsel or the petitioner, while Section 19 of the Act deals with penalties for violation of the provisions of the Act, Section 19-A of the Act deals with the cognizance of the offences and require that in order to enable the court to take cognizance, the Registration and Grievance Redressal Authority or any other officer authorized in this behalf to file a complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C.

The proviso is appended, wherein, when Registration and Mahammed Rafi S vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144980998/

Redressal Authority fail to take appropriate steps, any person who is aggrieved by such violation may file a written complaint.
Thus, in order to take cognizance, filing of complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. is necessary.
When the said mandatory requirement is not complied with, the continuation of the proceedings would amount to abuse of process of the court and as such, they are liable to be quashed.

9. However, having regard to the seriousness of the allegations made, it would be necessary to reserve liberty to the concerned authority to file complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. after which trial court shall proceed, in accordance with law and accordingly, the following;
ORDER i.
The petition filed by the petitioner/accused No.1 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C is allowed.

ii. The criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner/accused No.1 in crime No.230/2023 of Kudligi PS pending on the file of the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and JMFC, Kudligi for the offence punishable under Section 19(1) of the Karnataka NC: 2024:KHC-D:16539 Private Medical Establishments Act, 2007 is hereby quashed.
iii. However, concerned authority is at liberty to file complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C if so advised, after which trial court shall proceed, in accordance with law.
iv. In the event of filing such complaint, the period from the date of first information to the date of this order shall be deducted out of the period of limitation (if any).
